elaine: Quick question for the retest checklist — Compliance wants to ensure we never hand over raw customer PII to assessors. What is the minimal evidence package we can give that satisfies validation but keeps PII masked?
mike: For code/artifacts it's straightforward: sanitize logs, replace IDs with synthetic tokens, and provide a mapping only to sec-ops behind KMS if absolutely needed. For DB samples we should only provide schema + synthetic rows.
anders: On RBAC snapshot: we'll capture `aws iam get-account-authorization-details` output and include a generated CSV of principal -> permissions for the affected services. We should also record attached managed policies hashes. That way assessor sees who could do what without granting extra rights.
elaine: Good. Also product asked whether we can give assessors read-only listing of model artifacts (sha256 + metadata) but not the artifacts themselves. They want to verify model provenance. Is that acceptable?
mike: Yes — we can provide a manifest: `manifest.csv` with columns `artifact_name, sha256, created_at, version, sanitization_level`. No raw artifact. If an assessor needs to verify content, they can request a recorded decrypt via the KMS proxy flow.
sec-bot: [automated] Created ticket SEC-11001: "Retest evidence sanitization & RBAC exports" https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-11001
oncall: I'll schedule the infra snapshot 24h before the retest. Canary steps: 1) snapshot SGs & IAM details, 2) create `assessment-readonly-<ts>` role with tag assessment=true, session duration 2h, forced MFA, 3) mirror CloudTrail + VPCFlow -> s3://ret-test-evidence-1751234567/, 4) set object locking off for packaging.
anders: About the ephemeral role: session policy will restrict s3:GetObject only for `s3://ret-test-evidence-1751234567/metadata/*` and kms:DescribeKey on the `alias/ret-test-proxy` KMS alias. No decrypt. Example session policy I'll add to the ticket: ```json { "Version":"2012-10-17", "Statement":[ { "Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:GetObject","s3:ListBucket"],"Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::ret-test-evidence-1751234567/*" }, { "Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef12-3456-7890" } ] } ```
elaine: For KMS flow: we want the key policy to deny `kms:Decrypt` unless `aws:RequestTag/assessment` = `true` AND the request originates from the proxy role. We'll require the proxy to emit an audit blob (timestamp, requestor, sha256-of-plaintext) which we store in evidence bucket. No plaintext in logs.
mike: Operational note: rotate the `alias/ret-test-proxy` after the window and rotate the SSE-KMS key used for the evidence bucket. Also, presigned urls for assessor uploads should expire in 6h and require `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms`. Example upload: ```bash aws s3 presign s3://ret-test-evidence-1751234567/findings.json --expires-in 21600 ``` then upload with SSE.
anders: On verification: require these items before gating a retest slot: 1) RBAC CSV + IAM raw output, 2) manifest.csv with artifact checksums, 3) CloudTrail export sha256, 4) KMS key policy snapshot, 5) evidence-bucket manifest with SHA256 checksums. If any missing -> 48h hold.
elaine: Compliance also wants proofs that logs are unmodified. We can record a separate `cloudtrail-hash-<ts>.sha256` file containing a merkle root or just a concatenated sha256 of exported files. I'll add the command to the runbook.
oncall: We'll implement the mirroring as: ```bash aws cloudtrail create-trail --name assess-trail --s3-bucket-name ret-test-evidence-1751234567; aws s3 cp cloudtrail-exports/*.json s3://ret-test-evidence-1751234567/cloudtrail/; find cloudtrail -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; > cloudtrail-hash-1751234567.sha256; aws s3 cp cloudtrail-hash-1751234567.sha256 s3://ret-test-evidence-1751234567/metadata/ ``` and store the hash in the ticket.
mike: Also add an alerting rule: if `kms:Decrypt` is invoked in any unexpected context, page sec-ops and snapshot the proxy logs (retain 90d). Rate-limit decrypt proxy calls and alert >3/hour.
anders: For retest verification owner: whoever closes the verification step must upload a `verification.txt` signed by their internal SSO user (we can capture the username and timestamp) and attach it to the ticket. That gives us an auditable sign-off.
elaine: Owners: anders -> RBAC export + CSV, mike -> KMS proxy + key policy snapshot + alerts, oncall -> infra mirror + pre-window canary + rollback script, elaine -> compliance sign-off + evidence acceptance. I'll assign in SEC-11001.
sec-bot: [automated] SEC-11001 updated: assignees anders, mike, elaine, oncall; due date 2025-01-10
mike: I'll push the proxy PR to staging and attach the code sha256 to the ticket for reproducibility. Also adding a unit test that ensures no plaintext is logged.
elaine: Thanks. Final reminder to teams: scrub PII, use synthetic samples when demonstrating flows, and do not provide raw DB dumps under any circumstance. We'll run a tabletop on Tuesday to rehearse killswitch + retest gating.
anders: Will post the RBAC CSV artifact and `iam get-account-authorization-details` dump into the ticket after scrub.
elaine: ok closing loop. We'll do a 24h pre-window check in here. :white_check_mark:
